quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Look in your side mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
Look in your rearview mirror.
Stare straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that mirrors cannot show. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulders.

questions.question: When leaving a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well ahead of time. Start slowing down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway where stereo volume is restricted.
A television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the rear, and in the front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Your road ends ahead.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must turn either right or left.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive with the flow of traffic and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?

options.text: Drive slowly to let approaching vehicles and pedestrians move out of your way.
Honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren, pull over to the right curb or side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car if it blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
Some drivers must yield to other drivers.
Drivers should drive under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash on a black symbol means the action is forbidden. These signs are rectangular, white, with red and black markings.

questions.question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits in a collision.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. You must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes if you can do so safely. If you cannot change lanes, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You miss your exit on the interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. Continue to the next exit instead.

questions.question: This sign warns you of:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are a series of curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road has three or more curves coming up.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection and be ready to stop. Let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red light, you must stop completely and let other traffic go first.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights. Pull to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: To enter a freeway correctly, you should:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and merge at the same speed as other vehicles.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly to check the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and merge at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Use your signal and match the speed of traffic when merging onto a freeway. Always yield to other vehicles that are already on the road.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake suddenly to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often for tailgaters. If someone is following too closely, slow down gradually or change lanes to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake immediately during a blowout. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slowly release the accelerator and avoid braking. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the train has passed.
Under no circumstances.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train's whistle. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to come to a complete stop.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

questions.question: When driving in rain, which lights must you use?

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights.
Use parking lights.
Use no lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: What should you do when another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move over to the right, if there is an open lane to your right.
If there is not an open lane to your right, wait until the way is clear ahead and reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
Never slow down abruptly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If tailgated and there is a right lane, move right. If no right lane is available, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce speed. This will encourage the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a collision.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entrance to full parking lots.
Entrance to road construction areas.
Entrance to dead-end streets.
Entrances from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entrances from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic flows one way. You must not enter from your current direction.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and cannot see all the lanes because of oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before going ahead with your turn.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.
Edge your car into each lane of opposing traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before going ahead with your turn.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and safe.

questions.question: You are upset from something that happened at work. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
Stop at your favorite bar and have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
questions.explanation: Take time to calm down before driving if you are upset or angry. Letting emotions control your driving is poor judgment and dangerous to yourself and others.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror for traffic and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal when you change lanes.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no driver from either direction can cross it to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Wait for a safe opening before merging.

questions.question: To prepare for anything on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Scan the entire road and roadsides constantly.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting on the brake pedal.
Keep your focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the entire road and roadsides constantly.
questions.explanation: Good driving depends on spotting problems early. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Constantly scan the entire road, including both sides.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before braking.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden stops. When stopping, release the gas pedal first to slow your vehicle. Then apply steady brake pressure to stop smoothly and activate your brake lights.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, yield to that vehicle. Proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not immediately use the brakes.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, remove your foot from the gas. Do not brake immediately. Gradually slow your vehicle and gently apply the brakes before pulling over.

questions.question: How often must motor vehicles be inspected?

options.text: Once every four years
Once every three years
Once every two years
Once every year

questions.correctAnswerText: Once every year
questions.explanation: Vehicles must be inspected once per year during the owner's birth month. Schedule an appointment at an official inspection station.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough for others to know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough for others to know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before you pass so other drivers have time to know what you plan to do.
